name: Take a vacancy from advertisement through shortlisting and interview to an appointed member of staff
priorityReason: A staff record cannot be created for a new hire without an approved candidate, so nothing in the module starts without it.

goal.capability: to advertise a vacancy, shortlist, interview and put a candidate to the Principal
goal.outcome: the school appoints on a recorded process, and every applicant is answered rather than left waiting

Takes the final decision on every selection and rejection, and sets the joining date.
Sets the salary budget for the role when the vacancy is posted.

Delivers the interview invitation and the outcome to the address on each form.

additional.description: A candidate submits the application form on the school website.
The closing date passes and the applications are ready for review.

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin or Principal.
Accounts can set a salary budget for the role.

establishedBy.name: Setting and changing an employee's salary

preconditions.condition: The approval configuration for the outcome is set, or its default applies (BR-8).
An email channel is configured, since candidates are reached only by the address on their form.

postConditions: The vacancy was posted on the school website with its role and requirements, and Accounts set the salary budget for it at the same time.
Every application is recorded against the email address given on its form, with the CV attached.
A shortlist was drawn from the applications after the closing date.
Each shortlisted candidate was invited to an interview at a time either proposed by the system or set by the School Admin.
Interview marks are recorded beside each candidate's form and CV.
One candidate was selected and every other was marked rejected with a written explanation.
The Principal took the final decision and set the joining date, and no appointment was made without it.
The selected candidate was told their joining date and every rejected candidate was told the explanation recorded against them.
The approved candidate can now be converted into a staff record, and nobody else can.

dataFields.name: Role
dataFields.validation: The post being advertised. 2 to 100 characters.

dataFields.name: Requirements
dataFields.validation: What the school is looking for. 20 to 2000 characters.
dataFields.example: MSc Physics with at least three years teaching at intermediate level.

dataFields.name: Closing date
dataFields.validation: After which applications are reviewed. Not in the past (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Salary budget
dataFields.validation: The amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay. Set by Accounts when the vacancy is posted (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Email
dataFields.validation: The address on the form. Every application is recorded against it, and every message goes to it (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Shortlisted
dataFields.validation: Whether the candidate is called to interview (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Proposed slot
dataFields.validation: An interview time the system proposes. The School Admin takes it or enters one of their own (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Chosen slot
dataFields.validation: The time actually set for the interview.

dataFields.name: Interview marks
dataFields.validation: Recorded beside the candidate's form and CV, so the mark is read with what it was given for (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Outcome
dataFields.validation: Selected or rejected. Every candidate carries one (BR-9).

dataFields.name: Rejection explanation
dataFields.validation: 20 to 500 characters. Required for every rejection, and sent to the candidate (BR-9, BR-11).
dataFields.example: Strong subject knowledge but no experience at intermediate level.

dataFields.name: Joining date
dataFields.validation: Set by the Principal on approval (BR-10).
dataFields.requiredWhen: The candidate is selected and the outcome is approved

Set by Accounts when the vacancy is posted, and read later when the salary is agreed (BR-2).
One per candidate per vacancy, recorded against the email on the form, with the CV attached (BR-4).

permissions.rowScope: Own branch; may switch per branch-scope.
permissions.notes: Posts the vacancy, shortlists, schedules interviews, records marks and recommends the outcome. Cannot approve it (BR-8).
Takes the final decision on every selection and rejection, and sets the joining date.
Sets the salary budget for the role when the vacancy is posted. Takes no part in the selection.
Applies through the form on the school website. Holds no login and sees nothing else.

permissions.rowScope: No access. Applications carry other people's personal details.

businessRules.rule: A vacancy carries its role and its requirements, and is posted on the school website where candidates can find it.
Accounts set the salary budget for the role at the same time the vacancy is posted — the amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay. The agreed salary is later recorded against it.
Applications are reviewed after the closing date. A shortlist drawn while applications are still arriving is drawn from part of the field.
Every application is recorded against the email address given on the form, and every message to that candidate goes to it. A candidate reached at no other address must be reachable at that one.
The School Admin draws the shortlist from the applications and the CVs. Only shortlisted candidates are interviewed.

The system proposes interview timings, and for each candidate the School Admin either takes a proposed slot or enters a time of their own. A proposal that cannot be overridden is a constraint rather than a help.
Interview marks are recorded beside that candidate's form and CV, so a mark is read alongside what it was given for.
The School Admin selects and recommends; the Principal decides. The approval is configuration-based and the Super Admin can change who gives it, but the recommender is never the approver.
Every candidate carries an outcome. A rejection requires a written explanation, and a candidate left with no outcome at all has simply been forgotten.
The Principal sets the joining date on approval. An appointment with no start date is not an appointment.
The selected candidate is told their joining date, and every rejected candidate is told the explanation recorded against them. Both go to the email on the form.
Only an approved candidate can be converted into a staff record. That is the check the staff record use case performs.
An application is never deleted while the vacancy is open. How long a rejected candidate's application, CV and personal details are kept afterwards, and who may see them, is not decided.

transitions.condition: Posted to the website with its salary budget set (BR-1, BR-2).
Invitations are sent to the shortlisted candidates.
A selection and the rejections are recommended (BR-8).
Approved and the joining date is set (BR-10).
Returned with a reason. Nobody has been told.
The vacancy is withdrawn and applicants are told.
Converted into a staff record on joining (BR-12).

basicFlow.userAction: Creates the vacancy with its role and requirements and posts it on the school website, while Accounts set the salary budget for the role.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Posts it to the website and records the budget the agreed salary will later be measured against.

basicFlow.userAction: Applies through the online form, giving their name, father name and the other required details, and attaching their CV.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the application against the email address given on the form.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the applications and CVs after the closing date and draws up a shortlist.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Marks the shortlisted candidates. Only they are interviewed.

basicFlow.userAction: Takes a proposed slot for each candidate, or enters a time of their own, and sends the invitations.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sends a confirmation and interview invitation to the email address on each shortlisted candidate's form.

basicFlow.userAction: Records the interview marks beside that candidate's form and CV.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Stores the mark alongside what it was given for.

basicFlow.userAction: Selects the candidate to appoint and marks the others rejected, giving an explanation for each.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires an explanation on every rejection, and refuses to close with any candidate left without an outcome.

basicFlow.userAction: Takes the final decision on the selection and the rejections, and sets the joining date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the decision, which is what makes the appointment.
Tells the approved candidate their joining date and every rejected candidate the explanation recorded against them, at the email on their form.

alternateFlows.condition: The proposed slot does not suit
alternateFlows.behaviour: The School Admin enters a time of their own instead, since a proposal that cannot be overridden is a constraint rather than a help (BR-6).
They are rejected with an explanation at that point rather than left waiting, and are told when the outcome is approved (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal does not accept the recommendation
alternateFlows.navigation: Outcome approval → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to the School Admin with a reason. No candidate has been told anything (BR-8).
Another interviewed candidate is recommended and goes to the Principal in the same way. The declined candidate's outcome is recorded.

alternateFlows.condition: The vacancy is withdrawn before it closes
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every applicant is told rather than left waiting on a post that no longer exists (BR-9).
They are converted into a staff record. Only an approved candidate can be (BR-12).

exceptions.condition: The vacancy is posted with no salary budget
exceptions.messageShown: Ask Accounts to set the salary budget for this role before posting.

exceptions.condition: The closing date is in the past
exceptions.messageShown: The closing date must be in the future.

exceptions.condition: An application is submitted with no CV
A candidate applies twice to the same vacancy with the same email
exceptions.systemResponse: The second replaces the first rather than creating a duplicate (BR-4).

exceptions.condition: Shortlisting is attempted before the closing date
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused, since a shortlist drawn while applications arrive is drawn from part of the field (BR-3).
exceptions.messageShown: Applications close on 30 November. Review them after that.

exceptions.condition: An invitation cannot be delivered to the email on the form
exceptions.systemResponse: It is marked failed and listed, so a candidate who was not reached is identifiable rather than assumed invited (BR-4).
exceptions.messageShown: 2 invitations could not be delivered. See the list.

exceptions.condition: A rejection is recorded with no explanation
exceptions.messageShown: Give an explanation. It is sent to the candidate.

exceptions.condition: A candidate is left with no outcome
exceptions.messageShown: 3 candidates have no outcome recorded. Every candidate must be selected or rejected.

exceptions.condition: The School Admin attempts to approve their own recommendation
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Principal can approve a recruitment outcome.

exceptions.condition: The outcome is approved with no joining date
exceptions.messageShown: Set the joining date. An appointment with no start date is not an appointment.

exceptions.condition: A staff record is created from a candidate who was not approved
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused by the staff record use case (BR-12).
exceptions.messageShown: This candidate has not been approved for appointment.

departures.requirement: A vacancy cannot be closed while any candidate has no outcome, and every rejection carries an explanation that is sent. Nobody is left waiting.
Every message to a candidate goes to the address on their form, and a failed delivery is listed rather than assumed.
Applications carry other people's personal details and are reachable only by the School Admin and the Principal. No teaching or student role can see them.
How long a rejected candidate's application, CV and personal details are kept, and who may see them, is not decided. Until it is, they are retained and access-restricted.

openQuestions.question: How long is a rejected candidate's application, CV and personal details kept, and who may see them? The document flags this as not decided.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. Holding personal data with no retention rule is a liability.

openQuestions.assumption: Must reapply as modelled. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: What happens if the selected candidate declines after approval?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
